title: Minimum Size Subarray Sum >= target: variable window, shrink when condition met.
shortTitle: Minimum Size Subarray Sum >= Target: Variable Window, Shrink When Satisfied
keyPoints: Find the shortest contiguous subarray whose sum is at least target, over an array of positive numbers.
Grow the window by advancing right until the sum reaches the target, then shrink from the left while it still qualifies.
Record the minimum width before each shrink step, capturing the shortest qualifying window at each right position.
This is the shortest-valid pattern: shrink while the window is valid, record before shrinking.
The positivity precondition guarantees the sum rises when the window grows and falls when it shrinks, making the greedy shrink correct.
Amortized O(n) time because each element is added and removed at most once; O(1) extra space.
If negatives are present, the monotonic behavior breaks and you need a prefix-sum-plus-deque approach.

s1_definition.oneliner: Grow the window on the right until the sum reaches the target, then shrink from the left while it still qualifies, tracking the minimum length.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Minimum size subarray sum** – finds the length of the shortest contiguous subarray whose sum >= target, over positive numbers.
- **Variable-size window** – the right edge expands to grow the sum; when the sum meets the target, the left edge shrinks as far as possible while still qualifying.
- **Shortest-valid pattern** – shrink while the window is valid and record the width before each shrink.
- **O(n) time, O(1) space** – each element is added once and removed once; the left pointer only advances.
- **Positivity required** – all values must be positive for the greedy shrink to be correct.
s1_definition.analogy: The National Bank of India wants the fewest consecutive days in which Rajesh's deposits add up to at least a loan down-payment. Rajesh keeps adding days on the right until the total reaches the goal, then trims days from the left as long as the total still meets the goal, noting the shortest stretch that qualifies.

sections.s6_takeaway:
The minimum size subarray sum problem asks for the shortest contiguous stretch whose sum reaches at least a target, over positive numbers, and the variable-size sliding window solves it in O(n) time. You advance the right edge to grow the running sum, and the moment the sum reaches the target, you enter a shrink loop that trims from the left while the sum still qualifies, recording the width before each shrink.

This is the shortest-valid pattern, the mirror of the longest-valid pattern. In a longest-valid problem you shrink while the window is invalid and record after shrinking. Here you shrink while the window is still valid and record before each shrink. Knowing which direction the shrink condition points is what separates the two families.

The positivity precondition is essential. Positive values guarantee the sum rises when the window grows and falls when it shrinks, so the greedy shrink is correct. With negatives, this breaks and you need a different approach. The time is O(n) because each element is added once and removed once.

In a banking project at the National Bank of India, the loan desk uses this to find the fewest consecutive days in which a customer accumulated at least the required down payment, as evidence of saving discipline.

Remember one sentence: Grow the window until the sum meets the target, then shrink from the left while it still qualifies, tracking the minimum width, for O(n) time on positive arrays.
